 Order
Order No. 21.07.2023
02. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and the State.

2. By means of this application, the Petitioner seeks grant of anticipatory bail Under Section. 438 of Cr.P.C. in apprehension of arrest for his alleged involvement in the offences U/s. 417/
376(2)(n)/294/354/323/506/313/341/109/34 of IPC corresponding to C.T Case No. 191 of 2023 arising out of Raikia P.S Case No. 36 of 2023 pending on the files of learned J.M.F.C.,G. Udayagiri.
3. Perusal of the FIR reveals that the Informant has a love relationship with the present Petitioner since last two years.
On 20.03.2023, the present Petitioner assured her to marry and took her and kept in a rented house instead of taking her to his house.
He kept physical relation for fifteen days with the Informant.
Thereafter the Petitioner left the Informant and went to his house where his parents reside.

The Informant informed this matter to her // 2 // family members where upon they came and went to the house of the Petitioner in order to fix the marriage of the informant with the accused whereas all the accused persons abused them in obscene languages.
It is further alleged that during the last two years of their relationship, she got impregnated twice and was aborted twice by the present Petitioner.

4. Keeping in view the submission of the parties, the nature of allegations as emerged from the materials on record, the circumstances appearing, the seriousness and gravity of the offences, this court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the Petitioner.
Accordingly the prayer for bail Pradip Kumar Parichha @ Pradip vs State Of Odisha ....
